records.text: Owens said she believes Tyler Robinson picked up clothes and buried them at Dairy Queen.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: I certainly believe he did pick up clothes and bury them at Dairy Queen.

verification.notes: Transcript context confirms Owens expressed this belief. Current public charging and court materials say Robinson allegedly changed, removed, or hid clothing, but the research found no reliable public evidence that he picked up and buried clothes at a Dairy Queen. The underlying allegation therefore remains unverifiable and Robinson remains accused, not convicted.

records.text: Candace Owens said she believes Tyler Robinson was around the Utah Valley University campus, was at the Dairy Queen, and was depositing clothes, which could have been his part in the events.

appearances.snippet: I do believe that Tyler Robinson was around campus on that day. I do believe he was at the Dairy Queen, that he was depositing clothes, which could have been his part.

verification.notes: Owens frames this as her belief. Current hearing coverage reports prosecution surveillance that it identifies as Robinson on campus, but accessible official and reliable sources did not verify the specific Dairy Queen visit or alleged clothing deposit, and the preliminary-hearing identification remains contested.

records.text: Owens said the Dairy Queen screen grab carried a 6:38 p.m. timestamp, but the owner had not communicated that time to her team; they assumed the clock and time zone were accurate and should have disclosed that the time might not be precise.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Anyway, of course, when we documented this on our timeline initially and presented it to the public, we noted that the recorded timestamp of that captured screen grab was 6.38 p.m. ... I need to make it perfectly clear to you guys that we were not communicated that time by the owner of Dairy Queen. ... We assumed that it was correct at the time, which is to say we made an assumption that the surveillance cameras were updated and accurate and in the Mountain Standard Time Zone. ... So we didn't, we couldn't, we should not have given that information without making it clear that the time might not be precise.

records.text: Owens speculated that the Dairy Queen surveillance clock could have been inaccurate because of power loss or daylight saving time changes.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: So a couple of things that could have happened here, and these are both speculative, and we're going to speculate because that's what we have to do. ... A couple of options. One possibility is, of course, just we are all human. And for those of us that have worked at restaurants, outside of working somewhere that has a full-time security team whose job it is to keep equipment up to date, surveillance equipment... ... Easily could have fallen backward on time, backward or forward on time. Power goes out. It's daylight savings time. ... No one runs the clock backward or forward. There's a variety of common sense reasons and possibilities that lead to the plausibility that the camera time was just not accurately reflected in this small franchised restaurant.
